dns.title: DNS & Email Authentication
dns.summary: Missing or not found for neverssl.com: SPF, DMARC, DKIM, CAA.

findings.title: No DMARC record
findings.detail: Without DMARC there is no instruction for what a receiving server should do with mail that fails SPF or DKIM, and you get no visibility into who is spoofing you.
findings.recommendation: Start with _dmarc TXT: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain — read the reports, then move to p=quarantine and p=reject.

findings.title: No SPF record
findings.detail: Nothing declares which servers may send mail for this domain, so anyone can forge your address and receiving servers have no basis to reject it.
findings.recommendation: Publish a TXT record at the apex listing your senders, ending in -all. If the domain never sends mail, use: v=spf1 -all

findings.title: No CAA record
findings.detail: Any public certificate authority is allowed to issue a certificate for this domain. A CAA record limits that to the CAs you actually use.
findings.recommendation: Publish a CAA record, e.g. 0 issue "letsencrypt.org", plus an iodef address for violation reports.

findings.title: No DKIM key found at the common selectors
findings.detail: DKIM selectors are chosen by the sender and cannot be enumerated from DNS, so this is inconclusive — we probed 19 well-known selectors and none answered.
findings.evidence: default, google, selector1, selector2, k1, k2, dkim, mail, s1, s2, mandrill, zoho, protonmail, pm, sendgrid, mailjet, postmark, everlytickey1, fm1
findings.recommendation: Confirm with your mail provider that DKIM signing is enabled and the selector is published.

checks.note: Absence is inconclusive — selectors cannot be enumerated.
